title: International Pantry Staples for Pregnancy Nutrition
excerpt: Oats, Greek yogurt, lentils, low-mercury salmon, eggs, leafy greens, and citrus — practical ways to build balanced plates.
content:
## Introduction to Pregnancy Nutrition
Pregnancy nutrition plays a crucial role in ensuring the health and well-being of both mother and baby. During pregnancy, the body requires adequate nutrition to support the growth and development of the fetus. Therefore, choosing the right foods is essential.

## International Pantry Staples for Pregnancy
There are several international pantry staples that are beneficial for pregnant women, including:
- Oats: rich in fiber, which helps support digestive health and reduce the risk of constipation.
- Greek yogurt: rich in calcium, which helps support the development of the fetus's bones and teeth.
- Lentils: rich in protein, fiber, and other essential nutrients, which help support the growth and development of the fetus.
- Low-mercury salmon: rich in omega-3 fatty acids, which help support the development of the fetus's brain and eyes.
- Eggs: rich in protein, vitamins, and minerals, which help support the growth and development of the fetus.
- Leafy greens and citrus: rich in vitamins and minerals, which help support immune function and reduce the risk of illness.

## Building Balanced Plates for Pregnancy
To build a balanced plate for pregnancy, you can combine these pantry staples with other nutrient-dense foods. For example:
- Breakfast: oatmeal with Greek yogurt and fruit.
- Lunch: lentil soup with leafy greens and low-mercury salmon.
- Dinner: scrambled eggs with leafy greens and citrus.

## Food Safety Considerations
When choosing foods, it's essential to consider food safety. According to the [CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/food-safety/people-at-risk/pregnant-women.html), pregnant women should avoid eating:
- Raw or undercooked foods.
- Foods high in mercury.
- Foods contaminated with listeria.

## Conclusion
Pregnancy nutrition is critical for ensuring the health and well-being of both mother and baby. Choosing the right foods and following food safety guidelines can help support the growth and development of the fetus. You can visit our [meal planner](/blog/topics/pregnancy-meal-planner) for more information on pregnancy nutrition.

## Resources
- [WHO](https://www.who.int/tools/elena/interventions/nutrition-counselling-pregnancy): Nutrition counseling during pregnancy.
- [CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/food-safety/people-at-risk/pregnant-women.html): Food safety for pregnant women.
- [NHS](https://www.nhs.uk/pregnancy/keeping-well/foods-to-avoid/): Foods to avoid during pregnancy.

## Contact Us
If you have any questions about pregnancy nutrition, please contact us at [support](/support).

## FAQs
- Q: What foods are good for pregnant women?
A: Oats, Greek yogurt, lentils, low-mercury salmon, eggs, leafy greens, and citrus are all good options.
- Q: How can I build a balanced plate for pregnancy?
A: You can combine the pantry staples mentioned above with other nutrient-dense foods, such as fruits, vegetables, and whole grains.
- Q: What foods should I avoid during pregnancy?
A: According to the CDC, pregnant women should avoid eating raw or undercooked foods, foods high in mercury, and foods contaminated with listeria.
